meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots and dull skin in India**, the safest default choice is a **stable 10% vitamin C serum** used in the morning with sunscreen, because it balances effectiveness and lower irritation risk for most skin types.[1][7][16] If your spots are more stubborn and your skin already tolerates vitamin C well, a **15% serum** is the better step-up.[1][16]

If you want a practical short list from the results:

- **Best for beginners/sensitive skin:** **Pilgrim 10% Vitamin C Face Serum** with ethyl ascorbic acid and 5% niacinamide.[1]
- **Best for stubborn dark spots:** **Pilgrim 15% Vitamin C Face Serum** with ferulic acid and vitamin E.[1]
- **Best budget/visible pigmentation focus:** **Deyga 10% Vitamin C Face Serum** or **Minimalist 10% Advanced Vitamin C Serum** are both presented as strong value picks for pigmentation and glow.[10][5]
- **Best if you want maximum potency:** **La Roche-Posay Pure 12% Vitamin C** or **The Ordinary Vitamin C 23%** are highlighted for stubborn pigmentation, but the 23% option is more likely to irritate sensitive skin.[2][16]

What to look for when buying:
- **Vitamin C form:** ethyl ascorbic acid or L-ascorbic acid are the most commonly recommended forms for brightening.[1][16]
- **Strength:** **5–10%** if you are new or sensitive; **10–15%** for most people; **15–20%** only if your skin already tolerates actives well.[1][7][16]
- **Helpful add-ons:** **niacinamide**, **vitamin E**, **ferulic acid**, and **hyaluronic acid** can improve brightening support, stability, or hydration.[1][16]
- **Climate fit:** one result specifically argues **ethyl ascorbic acid** is a better fit for Indian heat and humidity because it is more stable than pure ascorbic acid.[3]

If you want one simple recommendation, buy a **10% ethyl ascorbic acid serum with niacinamide** if you are a beginner, or a **15% vitamin C serum with ferulic acid/vitamin E** if your main goal is faster dark-spot fading.[1][16]

If you want, I can narrow this down to **budget / mid-range / premium** options available in India.
